content:
# Sirach 28 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** Sirach 28 | **Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Total Disagreements:** 15

---

## Disagreement 001 — 28:1 "will-find vengeance / will receive vengeance"
**Verse:** 28:1
**EMET:** "will-find vengeance from-the-LORD"
**LOGOS:** "will receive vengeance from the LORD"
**PNEUMA:** "you'll get revenge back from the LORD"
**Issue:** εὑρήσει — "will find." EMET's "find" is literal. LOGOS's "receive" is interpretive (active gift from LORD). PNEUMA's "get back" loses the "find" nuance — vengeance finds you out. SOPHIA follows LOGOS as more natural.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "will receive vengeance from the LORD."

---

## Disagreement 002 — 28:2 "forgive your neighbor / forgive the wrong"
**Verse:** 28:2
**EMET:** "Forgive your-neighbor his-injustice"
**LOGOS:** "Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done"
**PNEUMA:** "Forgive your neighbor for what they did to you"
**Issue:** ἄφες ἀδίκημα τῷ πλησίον σου — "forgive the injustice to your neighbor." LOGOS adds "he has done" (not in Greek); PNEUMA adds "to you" (not in Greek). EMET is most literal. SOPHIA follows LOGOS for readability while noting the additions.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done you."

---

## Disagreement 003 — 28:2 "your sins will-be-loosed / will be forgiven"
**Verse:** 28:2b
**EMET:** "your-sins will-be-loosed when-you-pray"
**LOGOS:** "your sins will be forgiven when you pray"
**PNEUMA:** "your sins will be forgiven too"
**Issue:** λυθήσονται αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου — "will be loosed/released." EMET preserves the literal "loosed" which echoes Matthew 18:18 ("whatever you bind/loose"). This is theologically significant for the forgiveness theology. LOGOS's "forgiven" is standard but loses the "loosed" imagery.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "your sins will be forgiven when you pray" — "forgiven" is standard; but the note on λυθήσονται is preserved in the disagreement log.

---

## Disagreement 004 — 28:5 "being flesh / He himself being flesh"
**Verse:** 28:5
**EMET:** "He himself [being] flesh keeps-hold-of wrath"
**LOGOS:** "He, being flesh himself, holds wrath"
**PNEUMA:** "They're flesh and blood, and they're holding onto their rage"
**Issue:** σὰρξ ὢν — "being flesh." The point is the irony of a mortal creature maintaining wrath. PNEUMA's "flesh and blood" adds "blood" (not in Greek). SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "He himself, being flesh, holds on to wrath."

---

## Disagreement 005 — 28:6 "last-things / last things" and what they include
**Verse:** 28:6
**EMET:** "Remember your-last-things and stop-the-hatred; [remember] corruption and death"
**LOGOS:** "Remember your last things and cease from hatred; remember corruption and death"
**PNEUMA:** "Think about the end: death, corruption — and stop hating"
**Issue:** τὰ ἔσχατά σου — "your last things." The "last things" (eschata) is a technical term encompassing death, judgment, etc. PNEUMA specifies "death, corruption" and reorders them. SOPHIA preserves the technical term.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Remember your last things and cease from hatred; remember corruption and death and keep the commandments."

---

## Disagreement 006 — 28:8 "passionate-man / hot-tempered person / bellows for fire"
**Verse:** 28:8
**EMET:** "a-passionate-man kindles-strife"
**LOGOS:** "a hot-tempered person fans the flames of strife"
**PNEUMA:** "a hot-headed person is like bellows for a fire"
**Issue:** ἄνθρωπος ὀξύθυμος — "a quick-tempered/passionate man." LOGOS's "hot-tempered" and PNEUMA's "hot-headed" are both idiomatic. LOGOS's "fans the flames" is interpretive but apt given the fire context. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "the hot-tempered person fans the flames of strife."

---

## Disagreement 007 — 28:9 "cast enmity / throw enmity / throw quarrels like grenades"
**Verse:** 28:9
**EMET:** "will-cast enmity among those-who-are-at-peace"
**LOGOS:** "throws enmity among those who are at peace"
**PNEUMA:** "throws quarrels like grenades among people who were living in peace"
**Issue:** PNEUMA's "like grenades" is an anachronistic interpretive addition. The Greek ἐμβαλεῖ ἔχθραν — "will throw/cast enmity" — is direct. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "throws enmity among those who are at peace."

---

## Disagreement 008 — 28:12 spark/spit image
**Verse:** 28:12
**EMET:** "If you-blow on a-spark, it-will-blaze-up; and if you-spit on-it, it-goes-out"
**LOGOS:** "If you blow on a spark it blazes up; and if you spit on it, it goes out"
**PNEUMA:** "Blow on a coal and it blazes; spit on it and it goes out"
**Issue:** ἐπὶ σπινθῆρα — "on a spark/ember." PNEUMA uses "coal" for "spark/ember" — slightly different image. All agree on the rhetorical point. SOPHIA follows LOGOS ("spark").
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "If you blow on a spark it blazes up; if you spit on it, it goes out — and both come from your mouth."

---

## Disagreement 009 — 28:14 "third tongue" — exegetical note
**Verse:** 28:14
**EMET:** "A-third tongue has-shaken-loose many"
**LOGOS:** "The third tongue has shaken many loose"
**PNEUMA:** "The meddling tongue has sent shock waves through communities"
**Issue:** γλῶσσα τρίτη — "third tongue." PNEUMA abandons the term entirely, substituting "meddling tongue." The "third tongue" is a technical expression in Jewish literature for the slanderer/gossip — a "third party" inserted between two people. It must be translated literally and explained in notes. SOPHIA preserves the term.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "The third tongue has shaken many loose."

---

## Disagreement 010 — 28:17 "shatters-bones / shatters bones / breaks bones"
**Verse:** 28:17
**EMET:** "the-blow of a-tongue will-shatter-bones"
**LOGOS:** "a blow of the tongue shatters bones"
**PNEUMA:** "the tongue breaks bones"
**Issue:** συντρίψει ὀστᾶ — "will shatter/crush bones." "Shatters" is more forceful than "breaks." SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "but the blow of the tongue shatters bones."

---

## Disagreement 011 — 28:18 THE KEY VERSE — "not as many as have fallen because of the tongue"
**Verse:** 28:18
**EMET:** "Many-have-fallen by-the-edge of-the-sword, but not-as-many as have-fallen because-of the-tongue"
**LOGOS:** "Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not so many as have fallen because of the tongue"
**PNEUMA:** "More people have been destroyed by the tongue than have ever died by the sword"
**Issue:** πλείους — "more/most." This is the most quoted verse in the chapter. EMET/LOGOS preserve "not so many" (negative comparison); PNEUMA makes it a positive superlative. The Greek structure is negative: "not so many as." SOPHIA follows LOGOS's formulation precisely.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not so many as have fallen because of the tongue." — Preserved exactly as the chapter's key verse.

---

## Disagreement 012 — 28:19 "Blessed is he-who-has-been-sheltered" — the beatitude
**Verse:** 28:19
**EMET:** "Blessed is he-who-has-been-sheltered from it"
**LOGOS:** "Blessed is the man who has been sheltered from it"
**PNEUMA:** "Blessed is the person who's been shielded from it"
**Issue:** μακάριος ὃς ἐσκεπάσθη — "blessed is the one who has been sheltered/covered." "Sheltered" (passive, as if by God's protection) is the precise rendering. PNEUMA's "shielded" is slightly more militaristic. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Blessed is the man who has been sheltered from it."

---

## Disagreement 013 — 28:21 "Hades is-preferable to-it"
**Verse:** 28:21
**EMET:** "and Hades is-preferable to-it"
**LOGOS:** "and Hades is preferable to it"
**PNEUMA:** "better to go to Hades than to suffer it"
**Issue:** αἱρετώτερον αὐτοῦ ᾅδης — "Hades is preferable to it/than it." EMET and LOGOS render closely. PNEUMA adds "suffer it" (not in Greek). SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "and Hades is preferable to it."

---

## Disagreement 014 — 28:23 "Those-who-abandon / forsake the LORD"
**Verse:** 28:23
**EMET:** "Those-who-abandon the-LORD will-fall-into it"
**LOGOS:** "Those who forsake the LORD will fall into it"
**PNEUMA:** "those who have abandoned the LORD"
**Issue:** ἐγκαταλείποντες κύριον — "those abandoning/forsaking the Lord." Both "abandon" and "forsake" translate correctly; "forsake" is more traditional/covenantal. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "Those who forsake the LORD will fall into it."

---

## Disagreement 015 — 28:25 "balance and a scale / weigh them out"
**Verse:** 28:25
**EMET:** "for-your-words a-balance and a-scale"
**LOGOS:** "for your words a balance and a scale"
**PNEUMA:** "put your words on a scale and weigh them out"
**Issue:** ζυγὸν καὶ σταθμόν — "a balance and a weight/scale." Two instruments are mentioned: ζυγόν = balance beam, σταθμόν = counterweight/measure. PNEUMA reduces to one. SOPHIA retains both.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "and for your words a balance and a scale."
